messages:
maria: FYI rolling upgrade of Cilium from 1.14.0 -> 1.15.0 in eu-prod-gpu started, hitting issues. New GPU nodes join but show NotReady and kube-proxy in CrashLoop.
kevin: ugh. any error logs from kube-proxy? could be iptables vs ipvs mismatch after CNI change.
maria: kube-proxy logs show: \n```
I0512 10:05:12.123456 1 server.go:596] failed to start proxier: failed to init proxier: ipvs init failed: open /proc/net/ip_vs: no such file or directory
```
and Cilium post-install hook is restarting kube-proxy via a Helm pre/post hook. I'm seeing the helm hook run after the CNI CRDs, but before the ipvs modules are loaded on the node.
ashley: did we change kubelet args with the AMI bake? last bake added `--feature-gates=AllAlpha=false` but nothing for ipvs.
raj: Also seeing ArgoCD stuck in 'Syncing' for the cilium app: \n```
argocd-server: sync operation paused: failed to apply resource: timed out waiting for the condition
```
and the GitOps pipeline retries keep triggering the helm hook repeatedly.
ops-bot: terraform: Apply failed, state lock present: "Lock ID: tf-ops-92d3, Operation: apply, who: ci-cd-bot, version: 1.4.9". Manual unlock required or wait 10m.
maria: That's the other problem — Terraform can't expand the GPU nodegroup until we release the lock. Trying to scale now results in pending instances stuck in provisioning queue.
kevin: Quick mitigation: can we pause ArgoCD sync for cilium and roll back the helm release to 1.14.0 while we fix node bootstrapping? Rollback would skip the post-install hook.
ashley: +1. Rollback command: `helm rollback cilium 2 --namespace kube-system` (release revision depends). But be careful: CRD changes between 1.14 -> 1.15 could leave leftover resources.
maria: I'll pause argocd for the app: `argocd app set cilium --sync-policy none` and then run helm rollback on a canary subset (eu-prod-gpu-canary).
raj: Suggestion: modify the helm hooks to include `pre-upgrade` and add a `post-upgrade` that waits for `lsmod | grep ip_vs` or checks `systemctl restart systemd-modules-load` before touching kube-proxy. Also add a `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` annotation so CRDs apply in the right order.
kevin: Good call. Also we should update our AMI bootstrap to `modprobe ip_vs` earlier in cloud-init for GPU nodes — they're coming with a custom kernel and ipvs modules not enabled by default.
maria: For the Terraform lock: ci-cd-bot is running a plan on staging, I pinged infra-pipeline to abort and release lock. If not, we can `terraform force-unlock` but prefer not to.
ops-bot: CI pipeline aborted, lock released.
maria: Lock released. Starting canary rollback on eu-prod-gpu-canary now. Will tail the nodes and kube-proxy logs.
ashley: If rollback doesn't stabilize, we'll detach the new nodepool from the autoscaler and reprovision a clean AMI with ipvs modprobe in bake. We should add a preflight check in our rollout job that asserts `modprobe -n -v ip_vs` exit 0 before allowing the canary to proceed.
raj: I'll open a PR to add a preflight job in the GitOps pipeline and add the `sync-wave` ordering. Assigning to @kevin for AMI bake change.
kevin: on it. I'll also add a short-lived workaround in the helm chart to `sleep 10` in the hook while nodes settle (ugly but buys time).
maria: Update: canary rollback succeeded, kube-proxy restarted cleanly, new nodes become Ready. Rolling pause until we merge the preflight and AMI change. Thanks all :thumbsup:
argocd-bot: Application cilium paused by maria at 2026-05-12T10:20:00Z, sync disabled.
